tier_reason: The brepkit README Performance table carries every claimed number (brepkit-wasm 3.0.0 vs occt-wasm 3.8.3, measured 2026-08-07), and the harness is public (andymai/brepkit-bench bench.ts, exact-pinned package.json and lockfile, output-verified rows, median of 5 after 2 warm-ups), but no CPU model is stated and the brepkit-wasm wasm-opt settings are not given, so it cannot be A. All three pieces (brepkit, occt-wasm, brepjs adapter) are by the same author, so first-party C.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Rust 1.88+, cargo build -p brepkit-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --release (wasm-opt settings not stated). The current occt-wasm README states its build: emcc -O3 -flto -fwasm-exceptions with WASM SIMD (-msimd128, no relaxed SIMD), then wasm-opt -O4 --converge --gufa; it does not say whether the benchmarked 3.8.3 release (published 2026-08-03) used the same flags. Released npm packages exact-pinned in the brepkit-bench package.json and lockfile: brepkit-wasm 3.0.0, occt-wasm 3.8.3, brepjs 18.120.0, tsx 4.23.1; Node 20+.
corrections.caveats: First-party numbers: brepkit, the OCCT wasm baseline (occt-wasm) and the brepjs adapter used by both sides all come from the same author. CPU model not stated in the README (the harness prints it at run time but the published table omits it). Workloads are tiny primitives: the fuse row unions a box with a smaller box fully contained in it (touching three faces), so a containment fast path can dominate the 103x figure; volume(box) x100 measures an analytic box. Boolean and STEP rows are batches of ten. No native OCCT baseline; the brepkit native column has no OCCT counterpart. Numbers are for brepkit-wasm 3.0.0 and occt-wasm 3.8.3, both since superseded (4.1.49 and 5.7.0 on npm, 2026-10-11). The adapter paths are thin on both sides (direct k.fuse/k.cut/getVolume calls in brepjs src/kernel/occtWasm and src/kernel/brepkit), so adapter overhead looks comparable. Dual licence: AGPL-3.0-only or commercial from 3.0.0 on; versions through 2.129.x were MIT OR Apache-2.0.

notes: Numbers match the README table exactly; harness andymai/brepkit-bench/bench.ts verifies each row's volume (closed-form or cross-kernel) before timing, so no fast-but-wrong rows. Main shortcomings: same-author baseline build, no CPU model, trivial primitive workloads (fuse row is a contained-tool union), superseded package versions. Repo: 32 stars, 2,040 commits, last commit 2026-10-11, AGPL-3.0-only, not a fork.

tier_reason: The README micro-benchmark table shows the four claimed rows against MarchingSquaresJS.isoBands; the timing code appears to be example/index.html (single performance.now() call per case in a browser), with no hardware, browser or runtime stated, so first-party C.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: wasm-pack build; Cargo.toml [profile.release] opt-level = 3; wraps the contour 0.12.1 and contour-isobands 0.4.3 crates. Browser and wasm-bindgen versions for the benchmark not stated.
corrections.workload: Isoband computation on grids of 5,307 to 1,010,880 points with 14 to 23 intervals; the sizes match the cases in example/index.html (volcano 87x61 = 5,307 points, dem_big 336,960 points, dem_big concatenated three times 1,010,880 points; derived from page data). One cold call per library per case in the browser, timed with performance.now().
corrections.caveats: Micro-benchmark in the README with no hardware, browser or Node version and no link to the timing code; the matching code in example/index.html times a single cold call per library with no warm-up or repetition. The two sides run with different options: contour-wasm is called with use_quad_tree: false while MarchingSquaresJS.isoBands runs with its quadtree enabled (noQuadTree: false), and the wasm timed region also includes the Float64Array copy and a console.log of the result, so the comparison is not like for like (both asymmetries handicap contour-wasm). The vendored marchingsquares-isobands.min.js version is not stated. Speedup is 1.3x on the smallest input and 1.7x to 2.0x on larger ones. No commits since 2024-03-11. Licence AGPL-3.0-or-later is declared only in Cargo.toml and npm metadata; the repo has no LICENSE file.

notes: Numbers match the README (16 vs 12, 25 vs 15, 369 vs 186, 832 vs 492 ms; ratios 1.33x to 1.98x derived). Shortcomings: single cold run, no environment, mismatched quadtree option between sides, stale since 2024-03-11, licence only in package metadata. The algorithm lives in the author's contour-isobands crate; if that crate is listed elsewhere, treat this as its wasm wrapper. 5 stars, 25 commits, not a fork; npm contour-wasm 0.5.0 (2024-03-11, AGPL-3.0-or-later).

tier_reason: The README Performance table carries every claimed number; the benchmark code is public (src/__tests__/cosine.bench.ts, vitest bench) but no CPU, Node or browser version is stated, so first-party C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README row 'fast-theta (pre-normalized)', a bare dot product, vs full cosine similarity in the JS libraries. 384 dims: 3.3M ops/s vs cos-similarity 1.8M (1.8x), fast-cosine-similarity 1.4M (2.4x), compute-cosine-similarity 503K (6.6x). 768 dims: 2.6M vs 1.1M, 847K, 260K. 1536 dims: 1.8M vs 597K (3.0x), 414K (4.3x), 134K (13x) (ratios derived from page data). The like-for-like 'fast-theta (with normalize)' row is measured by the repo's bench but not published.
corrections.workload: Similarity of two random vectors at 384, 768 and 1536 dimensions in Node.js via vitest bench (src/__tests__/cosine.bench.ts); fast-theta gets Float32Array inputs (copied into wasm memory each call), the JS libraries get number[] arrays. The browser page bench/index.html compares only against an inline JS cosine function, not the npm libraries.
corrections.caveats: The headline row measures a bare dot product on pre-normalized vectors, while the JS libraries compute a full cosine similarity including both norms, so the comparison is not like for like; the repo's own bench also times 'fast-theta (with normalize)', the fair row, but the README omits it. fast-theta accumulates in f32 while the JS libraries use f64 doubles, so results differ in precision. No CPU, browser or Node version stated; baseline versions appear only as devDependency ranges (compute-cosine-similarity ^1.1.0, cos-similarity ^2.0.0, fast-cosine-similarity ^1.2.2) plus the lockfile. Licence MIT is declared in package.json and on npm (0.2.0) but the repo has no LICENSE file. 1 star, 25 commits.

notes: Numbers match the README; the benchmark is real but the published row is dot-product-only against full-cosine baselines (normalisation work skipped), f32 vs f64, and the fair 'with normalize' result is withheld. Low notability (1 star). Last commit 2026-02-27 (branch master), MIT via package.json only, not a fork.
